title: Python SDK: Structured model helpers and streaming ergonomics quickstart
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: ship a small, opinionated set of helpers in the Python SDK that make it trivial to 1) declare typed response models (dataclass + optional Pydantic validation), 2) hydrate partial/streamed responses into typed objects as chunks arrive, and 3) provide ergonomic retry and backpressure hooks for streaming consumers. This ticket is the engineering carrier for an end-to-end quickstart that will be used in docs and the examples repo.

Background: we have many internal patterns across runtime and examples that parse streaming JSON or chunked 'delta' events into complete objects. Teams want a supported SDK surface that reduces boilerplate and avoids reimplementing fragile merge/hydration logic. This should integrate with existing Python SDK streaming iterators and respect retry semantics (idempotency, resumption), plus make it easy to opt into Pydantic for stricter validation when users want it.

Non-goals: providing exhaustive schema generation from model weights, building a runtime-level retry/resume protocol, or supporting every 3rd-party validation lib. We provide a small surface and guidance for extensibility.
acceptance_criteria: New helpers available under redwood.sdk.models and redwood.sdk.streaming.hydrate (stable API in release sdk-2026.03)
Simple example shows: declare a dataclass, stream a chat-like response, and receive a final typed object after hydration
Streaming hydration supports incremental validation (best-effort) and final strict validation via Pydantic (opt-in)
SDK exposes backpressure hook that allows consumer to signal preferred buffer size and handles partial buffering correctly
Retry guidance doc and example showing idempotency token usage with resume semantics added to docs site
Unit tests cover merge logic, nullable fields, and chunk drop / duplicate chunk scenarios (>=90% coverage for helper module)
Bench indicates <5% added CPU overhead for common streaming paths compared to raw JSON parsing in our tests
design_decisions: Primary model type will be Python dataclasses for minimal runtime cost; Pydantic wrappers provided for users who want strict validation
Hydration model uses a deterministic merge algorithm: arrays appended, scalars replaced, and explicit 'partial' markers respected
Backpressure: expose an async TokenBucket interface on the stream that consumers may call to pause/resume; default behavior autosizes based on observed latency
Retries: library will not attempt automatic resume across server-side gaps; instead helpers will expose a resume token pattern and document recommended server impl
API ergonomics: iterator yields 'Event' union with types ['chunk', 'meta', 'error'] plus a hydrate() helper that converts accumulated chunks into typed model.
Keep the public surface intentionally small to avoid long-term maintenance burden
implementation_notes:
Planned files: sdk/redwood/models.py (dataclass base + helpers), sdk/redwood/pydantic_adapters.py (optional import), sdk/redwood/streaming_hydrator.py (async hydrator & backpressure hooks), tests/test_hydrator_*.py, docs/examples/streaming-typed-quickstart.md. Implementation will prefer minimal async primitives (asyncio) and avoid third-party dependencies besides pydantic which is optional behind an extras_require tag.

Key algorithm sketch:
- On chunk arrival parse JSON delta -> partial dict
- Merge into accumulator using merge rules
- Yield typed interim object only for 'meta' checkpoints if user requested interim validation
- Final hydrate(): run dataclass constructor; if pydantic enabled run model.parse_obj for strict semantics

Edge cases: out-of-order chunks will be detected by sequence numbers if present; otherwise fallback to last-write-wins for scalars and append for arrays. We will add telemetry to detect frequent out-of-order patterns and recommend server fixes.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: users expect automatic resume on network hiccups; mitigation: document clearly and provide example resume token pattern plus a follow-up ticket for server-side resume protocol
Risk: Pydantic dependency size; mitigation: make it optional and validate that docs call out optional install extras
Risk: Edge-case merge semantics causing subtle data loss; mitigation: run fuzz tests with representative delta sequences and include merge debug logs behind a feature flag
